plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Entire streets in Pretoria turn lilac-purple as these feathery-leaved trees burst into clouds of trumpet-shaped blossoms. Fallen flowers carpet the pavements in violet, making the city glow in early spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late September to November, with October the peak
plants.funFact: Jacarandas come from South America, yet Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of the tens of thousands of them lining its streets.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Goblet-shaped, six-petaled blooms rise straight from the bare ground in damp meadows, with no leaves in sight. Their pale pink-lilac cups bring a surprising flush of color just as autumn takes hold.
plants.location: Meadows and woodland edges across Europe (Northern Hemisphere autumn)
plants.funFact: Its leaves emerge in spring and die back, while the flowers appear months later in autumn. This is why it is also called 'naked ladies'. The plant is highly toxic and is the natural source of the compound colchicine.

plants.name: Sternbergia lutea
plants.description: Bright, golden, crocus-like goblets pop up less than six inches from the ground. They look like spilled sunshine on dry, rocky Mediterranean hillsides and in gardens.
plants.location: Mediterranean Europe and the surrounding region (Northern Hemisphere autumn)
plants.funFact: Despite its common name, it is not a true daffodil in the Narcissus genus. It is a relative in the same family, and it has adapted to flower after the long, dry Mediterranean summer.
